summary: Smart Logistics Global Ltd filed a Form 6-K to disclose its corporate governance practices as a foreign private issuer, confirming it will follow Cayman Islands rules in lieu of certain Nasdaq governance requirements, including annual meeting, voting rights, and shareholder approval rules. On June 12, 2026, Cayman counsel Appleby confirmed that the company's dual-class share structure—Class A shares with one vote and Class B shares with fifty votes each—is permissible under Cayman law. The structure was approved at the July 10, 2026 AGM. This is a routine corporate governance disclosure, not a special situation, but the dual-class adoption may affect governance dynamics. Watch for potential shareholder reactions to the multi-vote structure.
